items.title: Specializations of symmetric functions and the series $\sigma$
items.statement: Work in the algebra of symmetric functions over Q in an alphabet X, in which the power sums p_1,p_2,... are algebraically independent generators. A specialization is an algebra homomorphism f |-> f[A] to a commutative Q-algebra; it is determined by the sequence (p_k[A])_{k>=1}, and conversely every sequence of values gives one. For specializations A,B define p_k[A+B]:=p_k[A]+p_k[B], p_k[-A]:=-p_k[A] and p_k[AB]:=p_k[A]p_k[B]. For a coefficient multiplicity c write c dot A with p_k[c dot A]:=c p_k[A]. Distinguish this from a one-letter alphabet t, for which p_k[t]:=t^k and therefore p_k[tA]=t^k p_k[A]; all occurrences of tX, t^{-1} and sigma[t] below use this one-letter convention. The symbol 1 is the one-letter alphabet with p_k[1]=1, and -1 is its plethystic negative, with p_k[-1]=-1 (not the ordinary one-letter alphabet whose letter is minus one). Write f[A+B], f[-A], f[AB] and f[c dot A] for the corresponding specializations. Define X^perp to be the specialization with f[X^perp]:=f^perp for all f, where f^perp denotes the adjoint of multiplication by f with respect to the Hall inner product. Define the series sigma[X]:=sum_{n>=0} h_n[X]. Sigma is interpreted in the graded completion, or with a formal degree variable; every use of Hall pairing with a polynomial means its finite degree truncation. No convergence of a scalar infinite sum is asserted.
items.strategy: Existence and uniqueness of a specialization with prescribed p_k-values is the universal property of the polynomial ring Q[p_1,p_2,...]: the p_k are algebraically independent, so a homomorphism is specified by arbitrary images of the p_k and such a homomorphism exists. The operations on specializations are defined on the p_k and extended multiplicatively, again by the universal property. The adjoint f^perp of multiplication by f exists and is unique because the Hall form is nondegenerate and each graded piece of the symmetric function ring is finite dimensional (the Schur functions are an orthonormal basis). No choice is used. The adjoints of commuting multiplication operators commute: (fg)^perp=g^perp f^perp=f^perp g^perp. Thus the commuting algebra they generate is the target for the specialization X^perp; a noncommutative ambient endomorphism algebra is not being used as the coefficient algebra.
items.axiom_use: None: algebraic independence of the power sums over Q and finite-dimensional nondegenerate bilinear algebra.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); section 2.3 pp. 5-6 (lambda-ring formalism) and section 2.4 p. 7 (vertex operators (4)-(6))
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I sections 2-4 (power sums, complete functions, the Hall inner product)

items.title: Threefold Schur coefficients $c^\delta_{a,b,c}$
items.statement: For partitions delta,a,b,c with |delta|=|a|+|b|+|c| define the threefold Schur coefficient c^delta_{a,b,c}:=[s_delta] s_a s_b s_c, the coefficient of s_delta in the ordinary product of the three Schur functions. These are nonnegative integers, they are symmetric in a,b,c, and they satisfy the iterated Littlewood-Richardson identity c^delta_{a,b,c}=sum_phi c^phi_{a,b} c^delta_{phi,c}=sum_psi c^psi_{a,c}c^delta_{psi,b}, the sums over partitions phi (respectively psi) of |a|+|b| (respectively |a|+|c|). Equivalently c^delta_{a,b,c}=<s_a s_b s_c | s_delta>.
items.strategy: Nonnegativity follows from the iterated LR expansion below, and symmetry in a,b,c follows from commutativity of the product. The iterated identity is the associativity of the Schur product: s_as_bs_c = (s_as_b)s_c = sum_phi c^phi_{a,b}s_phi s_c = sum_{phi,delta}c^phi_{a,b}c^delta_{phi,c}s_delta, compared with the definition. The inner-product form is orthonormality of the Schur basis.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Section 2, equations (7)-(8), pp. 7-8 (the coefficients $c^\delta_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}$ of $s_\delta$ in $s_\alpha s_\beta s_\gamma$ and their iterated Littlewood-Richardson form)
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I sections 3 and 5 (Schur functions and their products, Littlewood-Richardson coefficients)

items.title: The Jacobi–Trudi completion $s_\mu$, the operators $U_n$ and $V$, and $\operatorname{stab}(\alpha,\beta)$
items.statement:
**Padded sequences.** For a partition $\alpha=(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$ and an
integer $n$, with missing parts read as zero, the first-row padding is the sequence
$\alpha[n]:=(n-|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$, a partition of $n$ exactly
when $n\ge|\alpha|+\alpha_1$
([[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]],
[[def-padded-kronecker-coefficient-sequence]]). When this sequence is used as
a partition label, omit trailing zero entries; in particular
$\varnothing[0]=\varnothing$ and the missing first part is zero.

**The Jacobi–Trudi completion.** For an arbitrary finite sequence of integers
$\mu=(\mu_1,\dots,\mu_m)$, define
$$s_\mu:=\det\bigl(h_{\mu_j-j+i}\bigr)_{1\le i,j\le m},$$
where $h_0=1$ and $h_k=0$ for $k<0$
([[thm-jacobi-trudi-and-dual-jacobi-trudi-identities]]); for the empty sequence
the empty determinant is $1$. Every such determinant is $0$ or $\pm1$ times a
Schur function. Indeed, put $q_j:=\mu_j+m-j$. If $q_j=q_k$ for $j\ne k$, the
$j$-th and $k$-th columns of the matrix agree, so the determinant vanishes.
Otherwise let $\sigma$ be the permutation sorting $q$ into decreasing order
$q_{\sigma(1)}>\cdots>q_{\sigma(m)}$ and set $\nu_j:=q_{\sigma(j)}+j-m$; then
$\nu$ is weakly decreasing and, permuting columns with sign
$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ and using
$h_{\nu_j-j+i}=h_{q_{\sigma(j)}+i-m}$, the determinant equals
$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\det(h_{\nu_j-j+i})$. If $\min_jq_j<0$ then
$\nu_m<0$ and the last column of this determinant is zero, so the value is
$0$; if $\min_jq_j\ge0$ then $\nu$, after deleting trailing zero entries, is a partition of $|\mu|$
with at most $m$ parts and the Jacobi–Trudi identity gives the value
$\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)s_\nu$. In particular $s_{\alpha[n]}\in\Lambda^n$
for every $n\ge0$, and $s_{\alpha[n]}=0$ for $n<0$: every term of the
determinant expansion has total degree $n$, so for $n<0$ some factor has
negative index and vanishes.

**The operators $U_n$ and $V$.** The Schur functions form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of
$\Lambda$ ([[thm-schur-functions-form-an-orthonormal-integral-basis]]), so there are unique
$\mathbb Z$-linear endomorphisms $U_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$) and $V$ of $\Lambda$
determined on the Schur basis by
$$U_n(s_\lambda):=s_{\lambda[n]},\qquad V(s_\lambda):=s_{\lambda+(1)},$$
where $\lambda+(1)=(\lambda_1+1,\lambda_2,\dots)$. Thus $U_n(\Lambda)\subseteq\Lambda^n$ for $n\ge0$ (and $U_n=0$ for
$n<0$), while $V$ raises degree by one; in particular $V(1)=s_{(1)}$. The operators
are extended linearly, and $V^k$ denotes the $k$-fold iterate of $V$.

**The stabilization index.** The internal product $*$ on $\Lambda$ is the
degree-preserving product of
[[def-internal-product-on-symmetric-functions]] and
[[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]. For partitions
$\alpha,\beta$, define $\operatorname{stab}(\alpha,\beta)$ to be the least
integer $n_0\ge0$ such that
$$s_{\alpha[n_0+k]}*s_{\beta[n_0+k]}=V^k\bigl(s_{\alpha[n_0]}*s_{\beta[n_0]}\bigr) \qquad\text{for all }k>0,$$
following the source. This definition records the source's convention only: it
does not assert that such an $n_0$ exists, nor that a value of $n_0$ satisfying
the display is least for any other property. Existence, least-ness and the
exact value of $\operatorname{stab}(\alpha,\beta)$ are proved in
[[thm-exact-global-stabilization-threshold-for-a-fixed-kronecker-product]].
items.strategy: U_n and V are well-defined by linear extension from the Schur basis, which is a Z-basis. The Jacobi-Trudi completion is well-defined by the published Jacobi-Trudi identities with the convention h_k=0 for k<0, and the sign statement is the standard column-permutation computation. The definition of stab(alpha,beta) only records the source's convention; no existence statement is claimed here. For the straightening assertion, take q_i=mu_i+m-i. If two q_i coincide, the corresponding Jacobi-Trudi rows (or columns in the transposed convention) coincide and the determinant is zero. Otherwise sort q decreasing; the sorting sign multiplies the determinant, and the new index sequence q_sorted_i-(m-i) is weakly decreasing. If its last part is negative, its final row has only negative h-indices and is zero; otherwise it is a partition after discarding zeros. This proves the claimed zero-or-signed-Schur rule, including invalid initial padding.
items.axiom_use: None: the Jacobi-Trudi completion and the linear extensions are Z-linear algebra on the free abelian group on partitions.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Introduction p. 4, equation (1) (Jacobi-Trudi determinant for an arbitrary integer sequence) and p. 5 (Definition of stab(alpha,beta) via the operator V); Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 8-9
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I section 3 (Jacobi-Trudi identities)

items.title: Schur functions on sums and products of alphabets
items.statement:
Let $A,B$ be specializations
([[def-lambda-ring-specializations-and-the-sigma-series]]).

- **(a)** For every partition $\lambda$,
  $$s_\lambda[A+B]=\sum_{\mu,\nu}c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}\,s_\mu[A]\,s_\nu[B],$$
  the sum over pairs of partitions with $|\mu|+|\nu|=|\lambda|$, where
  $c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ is the Littlewood–Richardson coefficient
  ([[def-littlewood-richardson-tableau-and-coefficient]]).
- **(b)** For every partition $\lambda$,
  $$s_\lambda[AB]=\sum_{\mu,\nu}g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}\,s_\mu[A]\,s_\nu[B],$$
  the sum over pairs with $|\mu|=|\nu|=|\lambda|$, where
  $g^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ is the ordinary Kronecker coefficient
  ([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]],
  [[def-internal-product-on-symmetric-functions]]).

Both sums are finite. No multiplicativity or bilinearity of $s_\lambda$ in
the alphabet variables, and no unproved Schur-functor decomposition, is
assumed.
items.strategy: (a) Use the published Schur Cauchy kernel: sigma[(A+B)Z]=sigma[AZ]sigma[BZ]. The left is sum_lambda s_lambda[A+B]s_lambda[Z]; expand the right as sum_{mu,nu}s_mu[A]s_nu[B]s_mu[Z]s_nu[Z], then use the proved LR Schur-product expansion in Z. Comparing the s_lambda[Z] coefficient gives exactly (a). (b) Use the same Cauchy theorem on sigma[ABZ]=sum_rho p_rho[A]p_rho[B]p_rho[Z]/z_rho. For fixed ordinary Schur functions f[A]=s_mu[A],g[B]=s_nu[B], their Hall pairing with this kernel is f*g in Z: in power coordinates f=sum a_rho p_rho and g=sum b_rho p_rho, the pairing is sum a_rho b_rho z_rho p_rho[Z], exactly the actual local internal-product normalization. The Schur expansion f*g=sum_lambda g^lambda_{mu,nu}s_lambda[Z] therefore gives the s_mu[A]s_nu[B]s_lambda[Z] coefficients of the kernel. Its Schur Cauchy expansion sum_lambda s_lambda[AB]s_lambda[Z] gives the other side of (b), so comparing coefficients proves (b). Every fixed Z-degree involves only finitely many partitions; these polynomial identities can then be evaluated at arbitrary specializations A,B. No multiplicativity/bilinearity of s_lambda in the alphabet variables or unproved Schur-functor decomposition is assumed.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); section 2.3 pp. 5-6 (lambda-ring formalism: s_lambda[A+B] and s_lambda[AB])
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I sections 2-5 (complete functions, Schur functions, the Hall inner product, plethysm)

items.title: The series $\sigma$: product formula, Cauchy identity, adjunction and reproducing kernel
items.statement: Let sigma[X]=sum_{n>=0}h_n[X]. (1) sigma[X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x)^{-1} and sigma[-X]=prod_{x in X}(1-x); in particular sigma[t]=(1-t)^{-1} and sigma[-t]=1-t for a scalar t. (2) sigma[A+B]=sigma[A]sigma[B] and, for the one-letter alphabet t, sigma[tA]=sum_{n>=0}t^n h_n[A]. (3) Cauchy identity: sigma[XY]=sum_lambda s_lambda[X]s_lambda[Y]. (4) For every specialization A the operator sigma[AX^perp] is the adjoint of multiplication by sigma[AX]: sigma[AX^perp]f[X]=f[X+A] for all f. (5) Reproducing kernel: <sigma[AX] | f[X]>_X = f[A] for all f.
items.strategy: (1) is the elementary product formula for the generating function of complete homogeneous functions, together with p_k[-A]=-p_k[A]; (2) is immediate from (1) and the multiplicativity p_k[AB]=p_k[A]p_k[B]. (3) is the exact Schur expansion of the locally proved thm-cauchy-kernel-has-power-complete-and-schur-expansions; its power expansion also supplies the kernel normalization used by the compatibility lemma. For (4) and (5): by Cauchy, sigma[AX]=sum_rho s_rho[A]s_rho[X], so multiplication by sigma[AX] is the operator sum_rho s_rho[A](multiplication by s_rho); for f=s_lambda and any g, <sigma[AX^perp]s_lambda,g>=<s_lambda,sigma[AX]g>=sum_rho s_rho[A]<s_lambda,s_rho g>=sum_rho s_rho[A] c^lambda_{rho,mu}=[s_mu]s_lambda[X+A] using the coproduct identity (a) of the previous lemma and orthonormality of the Schur basis. Taking g=s_mu shows (4); (5) is its equivalent dual form (evaluate on f=s_lambda and expand). The one-letter scaling uses p_k[t]=t^k, whereas coefficient multiplicity c dot A uses p_k[c dot A]=c p_k[A]; these operations are not conflated. The adjoint formula for arbitrary polynomial f involves only finitely many degree-lowering terms. Formal series and kernels are paired degree by degree; specializing a naked divergent scalar sigma[1] is never required.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); Lemma 2.1 and section 2.4, pp. 5-7 (the series sigma, Cauchy-type identities and the adjoint operator)
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I sections 2, 4 and 5 (complete functions, Hall inner product, adjoint operators)

items.title: Vertex-operator generating series for the padded Schur functions
items.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a partition and $t$ a formal variable. With the Jacobi-Trudi
convention of [[def-first-row-padding-completion-and-the-stabilization-operator]]
for the integer sequences $\alpha[n]=(n-|\alpha|,\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\dots)$, one
has an identity of formal Laurent series with coefficients in the symmetric
function ring
([[def-lambda-ring-specializations-and-the-sigma-series]]):
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}s_{\alpha[n]}[X]\,t^n=\sigma[tX]\cdot s_\alpha[tX-1] =t^{|\alpha|}\cdot\sigma[tX]\cdot s_\alpha[X-t^{-1}],$$
where $s_\alpha[tX-1]$ is evaluated through $p_k\mapsto t^kp_k[X]-1$ and
$s_\alpha[X-t^{-1}]$ through $p_k\mapsto p_k[X]-t^{-k}$. Equivalently,
$$\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}s_{\alpha[n]}[X]\,t^n =\sigma[tX]\sum_{\mu:\ \alpha/\mu\ \text{a vertical strip}} (-1)^{|\alpha|-|\mu|}t^{|\mu|}s_\mu[X].$$
items.strategy: Apply the Schur coproduct to the negative one-letter alphabet: s_alpha[tX-1]=sum_{i=0}^{ell(alpha)}(-1)^i t^{|alpha|-i} s_{alpha/(1^i)}[X], because s_nu[-1]=(-1)^{|nu|} for a column nu=(1^i) and is zero otherwise. The skew functions are the Hall adjoints e_i^perp s_alpha by def-skew-schur-function-by-hall-adjointness, and their determinants are supplied by thm-skew-jacobi-trudi-and-tableau-expansion. On the right, the coefficient of t^n in sigma[tX]s_alpha[tX-1] is sum_i(-1)^i h_{n-|alpha|+i}s_{alpha/(1^i)}. In the ordinary (non-transposed) Jacobi-Trudi matrix for (n-|alpha|,alpha), expand along the first row: its i+1-st entry is h_{n-|alpha|+i}, and deleting that column leaves exactly the skew Jacobi-Trudi matrix for alpha/(1^i), with sign (-1)^i. Equivalently expand the first column in the transposed convention printed in the Definition. Thus the coefficient equals s_{alpha[n]} for every integer n. Negative total degree gives zero: every nonzero determinant monomial would have that negative degree, impossible with h_k=0 for k<0. Homogeneity with the one-letter alphabet t gives s_alpha[tX-1]=t^{|alpha|}s_alpha[X-t^{-1}], so both generating formulas hold. All coefficient sums are finite; no scalar-divergent sigma[1] is evaluated.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); section 2.4, identity (6), p. 7 (the vertex operator series), and section 2.3 p. 6 (lambda-ring specializations)

Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Introduction p. 4, equation (1) (Jacobi-Trudi completion) and Lemma 2.1, identity (9), pp. 7-8 (Littlewood's vertex-operator identity)

items.title: The Jacobi–Trudi completion is compatible with the internal product
items.statement:
For partitions $\alpha,\beta$ put $a=|\alpha|$, $b=|\beta|$ and define
$$R_{\alpha,\beta}[Z]:=\langle s_\alpha[A]s_\beta[B]\,|\,\sigma[ZAB+ZA+ZB+AB]\rangle_{A,B},$$
the Hall pairing in the alphabet variables $A,B$
([[def-hall-inner-product-on-symmetric-functions]],
[[def-lambda-ring-specializations-and-the-sigma-series]]).

1. $R_{\alpha,\beta}$ is a finite symmetric-function polynomial in $Z$ of
   degree at most $a+b$.
2. For every integer $n\ge0$,
   $$(U_ns_\alpha)*(U_ns_\beta)=U_nR_{\alpha,\beta},$$
   where $U_n$ is the Jacobi–Trudi completion and $*$ the internal product
   ([[def-first-row-padding-completion-and-the-stabilization-operator]],
   [[def-internal-product-on-symmetric-functions]]); this holds for every
   $n\ge0$, including those $n$ for which the padded sequences $\alpha[n]$,
   $\beta[n]$ are not partitions. Equivalently, with $t$ a one-letter formal
   alphabet,
   $$\sum_{n\ge0}(U_ns_\alpha)*(U_ns_\beta)\,t^n =\sigma[tX]\,R_{\alpha,\beta}[tX-1].$$
3. The same polynomial is the finite Littlewood expression
   $$R_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_{\delta,\epsilon,\tau} \bigl((s_\delta s_\tau)^{\perp}s_\alpha\bigr) \bigl((s_\epsilon s_\tau)^{\perp}s_\beta\bigr) \bigl(s_\delta*s_\epsilon\bigr),$$
   the sum over all triples of partitions, all factors evaluated at $Z$.
items.strategy: First establish the internal-product kernel from the actual published normalization p_rho*p_tau=delta_{rho,tau} z_rho p_rho and <p_rho,p_tau>=delta_{rho,tau} z_rho: for homogeneous f,g of the same degree, <f[A]g[B] | sigma[XAB]>_{A,B}=f*g in X, by the power expansion sigma[XAB]=sum_rho p_rho[X]p_rho[A]p_rho[B]/z_rho; unequal degrees pair to zero. Write f=s_alpha, g=s_beta. The padded vertex series has A-degree-n component U_n f in sigma[A]f[A-1] and B-degree-n component U_n g in sigma[B]g[B-1]. Therefore F(t):=sum_n(U_n f)*(U_n g)t^n=<sigma[A]f[A-1] sigma[B]g[B-1] | sigma[tXAB]>_{A,B}. Move multiplication by sigma[A] and sigma[B] to the kernel by Hall adjunction: translate A and B each by the one-letter 1, obtaining <f[A-1]g[B-1] | sigma[tX(A+1)(B+1)]>. Moving the two negative translations on f,g to the kernel multiplies it by sigma[-A]sigma[-B]. Factor out sigma[tX], and multiplicativity of sigma gives F(t)=sigma[tX]<f[A]g[B] | sigma[tXAB+tXA+tXB-A-B]>. On setting Z=tX-1 in ZAB+ZA+ZB+AB, the negative AB term from ZAB cancels the positive AB, leaving exactly tXAB+tXA+tXB-A-B. Hence F(t)=sigma[tX]R[tX-1]. Finiteness of R: in the factorization sigma[ZAB]sigma[ZA]sigma[ZB]sigma[AB], terms with degrees i,j,k,l satisfy i+j+l=a and i+k+l=b; Z-degree i+j+k=a+b-i-2l<=a+b. Only finitely many indices and partitions contribute. The vertex formula applied linearly to this finite R identifies the coefficient of t^n as U_nR. Every manipulation is degree-by-degree: for fixed t^n the first kernel has A/B-degree n, and the shifted kernel has A/B-degree at most n; polynomial f,g or the fixed-degree components bound the remaining pairings. No scalar sum sigma[1] or analytic convergence is evaluated, and no unproved Littlewood identity or current-rank injectivity is assumed. To identify the classical Littlewood expression, expand sigma[AB]=sum_tau s_tau[A]s_tau[B], sigma[ZA]=sum_theta s_theta[Z]s_theta[A] and sigma[ZB]=sum_pi s_pi[Z]s_pi[B], and use the proved triple internal-product kernel on sigma[ZAB]. The Hall coefficients in A and B are <s_alpha,s_delta s_tau s_theta> and <s_beta,s_epsilon s_tau s_pi>. Reproducing in Z identifies their sums over theta and pi with (s_delta s_tau)^perp s_alpha and (s_epsilon s_tau)^perp s_beta, while the remaining Z-factor is s_delta*s_epsilon. This gives exactly the finite Littlewood sum printed in BOR (9), with its compatibility now proved rather than cited.
items.axiom_use: None: rational finite-degree power-sum/Hall algebra and formal coefficient extraction; no infinite choice.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Lemma 2.1 and Littlewood's identity (9), pp. 7-8 (the element R_{alpha,beta}, the operator U_n, and the Littlewood sum)
Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); section 2.4, identity (6), p. 7 (vertex operator series)

items.title: Murnaghan stability for Kronecker coefficients
items.statement:
Fix partitions $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ and work over a field $k$ of
characteristic $0$, with $V_\lambda$ denoting the irreducible $kS_n$-module
of shape $\lambda\vdash n$
([[lem-specht-modules-classify-irreducibles-over-characteristic-zero-fields]]).
Put $m(\gamma):=\max\{|\alpha|+\alpha_1,\,|\beta|+\beta_1,\,|\gamma|+\gamma_1\}$
and, for $n\ge m(\gamma)$, let
$$g_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):=g^{\gamma[n]}_{\alpha[n],\beta[n]}$$
be the multiplicity of $V_{\gamma[n]}$ in
$V_{\alpha[n]}\otimes V_{\beta[n]}$
([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]],
[[def-padded-kronecker-coefficient-sequence]]); set
$g_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma):=0$ for $n<m(\gamma)$, where the padded sequences
are not partitions.

Then the sequence $n\mapsto g_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ is eventually constant.
More precisely, there is a finite set $S(\alpha,\beta)$ of partitions and
nonnegative integers $\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}$ for $\gamma\in S(\alpha,\beta)$,
with $\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}:=0$ for $\gamma\notin S(\alpha,\beta)$, such
that $g_n(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)=\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}$ for all
sufficiently large $n$ and every partition $\gamma$. No explicit bound on the
stable rank is asserted here; the sharp global bound is a separate claim.
items.strategy: FI-module route of Church-Ellenberg-Farb. By CEF Proposition 3.4.1 the assignments V(alpha)_n:=V_{alpha[n]} for n>=|alpha|+alpha_1 and V(alpha)_n:=0 below define a finitely generated FI-module. By CEF Proposition 2.3.6 the tensor product V(alpha)(x)V(beta) is finitely generated and its value in rank n is V_{alpha[n]} (x) V_{beta[n]}. CEF Theorem 1.13 states that a finitely generated FI-module over a field of characteristic 0 is uniformly representation stable: there is a finite set of partitions nu and fixed multiplicities c_nu such that the rank-n value is the direct sum of c_nu copies of V(nu)_n for all n in a stable range. Restricting to the single irreducible family nu=gamma and reading off multiplicities gives the eventual constancy of n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma); the finiteness of the support is the finiteness of the constituent list. All inputs are the in-run suppliers named in deps; the argument is choice-free. The corrected batch27 rational-model weight Definition, finite-orbit restriction proof and padded-family supplier retain the exact finite-dimensional complex Specht interfaces used here. Tensor rank n is the product of the two distinct families alpha and beta. The finite constituent support and uniform fixed multiplicities come from the finite-generation/stability equivalence, without using the later all-rank identity or sharp threshold.
items.axiom_use: None: the proof is finite-dimensional representation theory over a characteristic-zero field plus the choice-free FI-module finite-generation machinery of the cited suppliers.

references.title: Thomas Church, Jordan S. Ellenberg and Benson Farb, FI-modules and stability for representations of symmetric groups, arXiv:1204.4533v4 (2014); Proposition 3.4.1 pp. 23-24, Proposition 2.3.6 pp. 12-13, Theorem 1.13 pp. 6-7
Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Murnaghan's theorem, p. 4

items.title: The reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient $\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}$
items.statement: For partitions alpha, beta, gamma define the reduced (stable) Kronecker coefficient bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} to be the eventual value of the padded sequence n |-> g_n(alpha,beta,gamma) furnished by the Murnaghan stability theorem; equivalently bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} := lim_{n to infinity} g^{gamma[n]}_{alpha[n],beta[n]}, where the sequence is defined for n>=max{|alpha|+alpha_1,|beta|+beta_1,|gamma|+gamma_1} and set to 0 below. Well-definedness is exactly the Murnaghan stability theorem. Two immediate conventions: bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=bar-g^gamma_{beta,alpha} (commutativity of the tensor product), and for fixed alpha,beta only finitely many gamma have bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} nonzero. Values used later and verified in the source's introduction for alpha=beta=(2): bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 and bar-g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1.
items.strategy: Well-definedness is the preceding theorem: the eventual constant of an eventually constant sequence of nonnegative integers is a unique nonnegative integer, no choice is involved. The symmetry in alpha,beta is the commutativity of the tensor product of representations. The two displayed values are read from the source's introduction's product table and are not used as logical inputs.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Introduction pp. 2 and 5 (definition of the reduced Kronecker coefficients) and the displayed product table p. 2

items.title: Brion's formula for the reduced Kronecker coefficients
items.statement:
For all partitions $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$,
$$\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta} =\bigl\langle s_\alpha[X]s_\beta[Y]\,\big|\,\sigma[XY]\,s_\gamma[XY+X+Y]\bigr\rangle_{X,Y},$$
the inner product being the Hall inner product extended to symmetric functions
in the two alphabet variables $X,Y$, and $\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}$ the
reduced Kronecker coefficient
([[def-reduced-kronecker-coefficient]]).

Equivalently, introducing a third alphabet $Z$,
$$\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma}\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}\, s_\alpha[X]s_\beta[Y]s_\gamma[Z] =\sigma[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ],$$
the symmetric Cauchy-type identity for the reduced coefficients, summed over
all triples of partitions and by total degree. Equivalently again, in the
notation of
[[lem-padding-completion-is-compatible-with-the-internal-product]],
$$R_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma \bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}\,s_\gamma,$$
the finite Schur expansion of the polynomial $R_{\alpha,\beta}$.
items.strategy: Define R_{alpha,beta}[Z]=<s_alpha[A]s_beta[B] | sigma[ZAB+ZA+ZB+AB]>_{A,B}, the finite polynomial of the padding/internal-product compatibility lemma. That lemma proves the complete all-n identity (U_n s_alpha)*(U_n s_beta)=U_n R without using reduced coefficients. Expand R=sum_gamma r_gamma s_gamma with finite support of degree at most |alpha|+|beta|. Choose n sufficiently large that alpha[n], beta[n] and every gamma[n] in both this finite support and the FI-stable finite support are partitions. Distinct gamma have distinct tails, hence distinct padded Schur labels. Comparing the compatibility identity with the FI-stable expansion identifies r_gamma with bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}; this uses injectivity only at sufficiently large n, not at every admissible n. To compute r_gamma, factor the kernel as sigma[AB] sigma[Z(AB+A+B)] and apply Cauchy in Z: the coefficient of s_gamma[Z] is sigma[AB]s_gamma[AB+A+B]. Pairing with s_alpha[A]s_beta[B] gives exactly the claimed Brion formula. Reproducing in the three alphabets yields the symmetric sigma[XYZ+XY+XZ+YZ] identity. No Littlewood identity, geometric result or unproved vertex compatibility is imported.
items.axiom_use: None: the proof uses the lambda-ring calculus, Cauchy's identity and formal power series in one variable over a characteristic-zero algebra.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); Proposition 3.2 and identity (10), pp. 9-10 (Brion's formula and the symmetric Cauchy-type identity)
Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Murnaghan's theorem p. 4 and Lemma 2.1 pp. 7-8

items.title: The nonnegative expansion of a reduced Kronecker coefficient
items.statement: For all partitions alpha,beta,gamma one has the finite nonnegative expansion bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta} = sum_{mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi} c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi} c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta} c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} g^mu_{lambda,eta}, the sum over all six-tuples of partitions (only finitely many summands are nonzero), where the c's are threefold Schur coefficients and the g's are ordinary Kronecker coefficients. Consequences: (i) bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 if and only if there exist partitions mu,lambda,eta,rho,theta,pi with c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi}, c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta}, c^beta_{rho,eta,pi} and g^mu_{lambda,eta} all positive; (ii) for every nonzero summand the degree equations |alpha|=|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|, |beta|=|rho|+|eta|+|pi|, |gamma|=|mu|+|theta|+|pi| and |mu|=|lambda|=|eta| hold; (iii) for fixed alpha,beta the index set is finite because rho,lambda,theta are contained in alpha, rho,eta,pi in beta, and |mu|=|lambda|. All summands are nonnegative integers, so no cancellation occurs.
items.strategy: Expand Brion's formula in the two alphabets X,Y: sigma[XY] = sum_rho s_rho[X]s_rho[Y] by Cauchy, and s_gamma[XY+X+Y] = sum_{mu,nu} c^gamma_{mu,nu} s_mu[XY] s_nu[X+Y] by the coproduct identity, then s_mu[XY] = sum_{lambda,eta} g^mu_{lambda,eta} s_lambda[X]s_eta[Y] and s_nu[X+Y] = sum_{theta,pi} c^nu_{theta,pi}s_theta[X]s_pi[Y] by the coproduct and plethysm identities. The right-hand side becomes sum c^gamma_{mu,nu} c^nu_{theta,pi} g^mu_{lambda,eta} s_rho s_lambda s_theta[X] s_rho s_eta s_pi[Y]; the coefficient of s_alpha[X]s_beta[Y] is sum over rho,lambda,theta of c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta} (respectively rho,eta,pi) times the rest. Using the iterated identity sum_nu c^gamma_{mu,nu}c^nu_{theta,pi}=c^gamma_{mu,theta,pi} gives the displayed formula. Consequences (i),(ii) are the positivity and degree bookkeeping of the individual summands (the supports of threefold coefficients and of g are governed by containment and total degree). This proves the source's Lemma 2.1 in the derived index pattern; the source's displayed equality (8) prints a third-factor index set that is a typographical variant of the same K_4 index pattern (the version proved here is the one used by the source's proof and by their if-and-only-if statement).
items.axiom_use: None: the expansion is an elementary computation in the lambda-ring with Cauchy's identity and the coproduct/plethysm identities; all coefficients are nonnegative integers.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Lemma 2.1 and equation (8), pp. 7-8 (nonnegative expansion of the reduced coefficients)
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I sections 3 and 5 (Littlewood-Richardson coefficients)

items.title: The Murnaghan expansion at every admissible rank
items.statement:
For all partitions $\alpha,\beta$ and every integer
$n\ge\max\{|\alpha|+\alpha_1,\,|\beta|+\beta_1\}$:
$$s_{\alpha[n]}*s_{\beta[n]}=\sum_\gamma \bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}\,s_{\gamma[n]},$$
an identity in the symmetric function ring, where $s_{\gamma[n]}$ is the
Jacobi–Trudi determinant attached to the integer sequence
$\gamma[n]=(n-|\gamma|,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\dots)$, equal to $0$ or $\pm1$ times
a Schur function
([[def-first-row-padding-completion-and-the-stabilization-operator]],
[[def-first-row-padding-of-a-partition]]), and $*$ is the internal product
([[def-kronecker-coefficient-and-internal-tensor-product]]).

For an ordinary partition $\delta\vdash n$ the coefficient of $s_\delta$ is
$$g^\delta_{\alpha[n],\beta[n]} =\sum_\gamma \bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}\, \langle s_{\gamma[n]},s_\delta\rangle_H,$$
where each Hall factor is $0$ or a sign coming from Jacobi–Trudi
straightening ([[thm-schur-functions-form-an-orthonormal-integral-basis]]).
At small admissible ranks the signed terms can cancel or coalesce;
individual coefficients need not yet equal their reduced values. The range
displayed is precisely the set of $n$ for which $\alpha[n]$ and $\beta[n]$
are partitions.
items.strategy: The local padding/internal-product compatibility lemma proves (U_n s_alpha)*(U_n s_beta)=U_n R_{alpha,beta} coefficient by coefficient for every n>=0, with R finite. Brion identifies R=sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}s_gamma by comparison only at sufficiently large n where every finite-support gamma[n] is an ordinary partition and labels are distinct. Apply the same linear U_n at the present n, without requiring injectivity: its definition gives U_n R=sum_gamma bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}s_{gamma[n]}. In the admissible range the left inputs are ordinary Schur functions, so this is the promised full all-rank identity. Pair with each ordinary s_delta for the exact signed coefficient formula. For example alpha=beta=gamma=(2), n=4 gives ordinary coefficient 1 although the reduced coefficient is 2; straightening s_(1,3)=-s_(2,2) supplies the missing cancellation in the complete expansion. No coefficientwise stability is asserted before the actual stable range.
items.axiom_use: None: finite Hall coefficient extraction, proved vertex/Hall compatibility and linear Jacobi-Trudi completion suffice.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Murnaghan Theorem (2) p. 4, Example 1 p. 4 and Lemma 2.1 pp. 7-8
Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); section 2.3 pp. 5-6

items.title: Murnaghan–Littlewood: top-degree reduced coefficients are Littlewood–Richardson coefficients
items.statement: Let alpha,beta,gamma be partitions with |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta|. Then bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}=c^gamma_{alpha,beta}, the Littlewood-Richardson coefficient. In particular bar-g^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=c^{alpha+beta}_{alpha,beta}=1.
items.strategy: Apply the nonnegative expansion of the preceding lemma. For every nonzero summand the degree equations give |alpha|+|beta|-|gamma| = (|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|)+(|rho|+|eta|+|pi|)-(|mu|+|theta|+|pi|) = 2|rho|+|lambda|+|eta|-|mu| = 2|rho|+|mu|, using |lambda|=|eta|=|mu|. If |gamma|=|alpha|+|beta| then 2|rho|+|mu|=0, so rho=mu=empty; then |lambda|=|eta|=0, so lambda=eta=empty; hence c^alpha_{rho,lambda,theta}=c^alpha_{empty,empty,theta}=delta_{alpha,theta} and c^beta_{empty,empty,pi}=delta_{beta,pi}, and the six-fold sum collapses to the single summand g^empty_{empty,empty} c^gamma_{alpha,beta} = c^gamma_{alpha,beta}. For gamma=alpha+beta the LR coefficient equals 1: the Pieri/LR rule gives the unique Littlewood-Richardson tableau of shape (alpha+beta)/alpha whose row i is filled with i's. The row-i filling is lattice because beta is weakly decreasing. Any LR tableau has only 1s in its first skew row, which has beta_1 boxes and exhausts that content; inductively each successive row exhausts the next content, so the filling is unique. Empty rows/partitions use zero content and the unique empty tableau.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Murnaghan–Littlewood Theorem, p. 4
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I §5 (Littlewood-Richardson rule)

items.title: The support of the reduced Kronecker coefficients satisfies the size triangle inequalities
items.statement: If bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0 then |alpha| <= |beta|+|gamma|, |beta| <= |alpha|+|gamma| and |gamma| <= |alpha|+|beta| (Murnaghan's inequalities). Hence the support Supp(alpha,beta) of the nonzero reduced coefficients with fixed alpha,beta lies in the triangle region of the weight lattice.
items.strategy: Take a nonzero summand of the nonnegative expansion and use its degree equations |alpha|=|rho|+|lambda|+|theta|, |beta|=|rho|+|eta|+|pi|, |gamma|=|mu|+|theta|+|pi| with |lambda|=|eta|=|mu|. Subtracting pairwise: |alpha|+|beta|-|gamma| = 2|rho|+|mu| >= 0; |alpha|+|gamma|-|beta| = |lambda|+2|theta|+|mu|-|eta| = 2|theta|+|mu| >= 0; |beta|+|gamma|-|alpha| = 2|pi|+|mu| >= 0. Each difference is a sum of nonnegative integers, giving the three inequalities for that summand, hence for their positive sum.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Murnaghan's inequalities, p. 4

items.title: The exact global stabilization threshold for a fixed Kronecker product
items.statement:
For all partitions $\alpha,\beta$ with missing parts read as zero,
$$\operatorname{stab}(\alpha,\beta)=N:=|\alpha|+|\beta|+\alpha_1+\beta_1,$$
with $\operatorname{stab}$ as in
[[def-first-row-padding-completion-and-the-stabilization-operator]].

More precisely. At every $n\ge N$ all support labels $\gamma[n]$ of the
finite support of $\bar g^\bullet_{\alpha,\beta}$ are ordinary partitions, the
full product has the fixed nonnegative Schur expansion
$s_{\alpha[n]}*s_{\beta[n]}=\sum_\gamma\bar g^\gamma_{\alpha,\beta}s_{\gamma[n]}$,
and the family is $V$-stable from $N$ onward. If both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are
nonempty, $N-1$ is admissible and the product at $N$ is not $V$ of the product
at $N-1$: the coefficient of $s_{(\alpha+\beta)[N]}$ is $1$, its first two
parts are equal, and no such Schur basis vector lies in the image of $V$. If
exactly one input is empty, $N$ is already the least ordinary input rank, and
the same image obstruction at $N$ excludes any earlier stabilization index in
the Jacobi–Trudi convention of the Definition. If both inputs are empty,
$N=0$, $s_{(n)}*s_{(n)}=s_{(n)}$ (including $s_{(0)}=1$) and $V^n(1)=s_{(n)}$,
so stabilization begins at zero and no negative-rank product is invoked. No
sharpness for an individual coefficient is claimed.
items.strategy: Source route: Briand-Orellana-Rosas Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, pp. 8-9. (i) Support maximum: every nonzero summand of the nonnegative expansion satisfies |gamma|+gamma_1 <= |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1 - the chain is |gamma|+gamma_1 <= |mu|+mu_1+|theta|+theta_1+|pi|+pi_1 <= 2|mu|+|theta|+theta_1+|pi|+pi_1 = |lambda|+|theta|+theta_1+|eta|+|pi|+pi_1 <= |alpha|+alpha_1+|beta|+beta_1, using the threefold containment theta subset alpha, pi subset beta, the row bound gamma_1 <= mu_1+theta_1+pi_1 from the LR rule, mu_1 <= |mu|, |mu|=|lambda|=|eta| and |lambda|+|theta| <= |alpha|, |eta|+|pi| <= |beta|; combined with the top-degree lemma, which shows that gamma=alpha+beta attains the value |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1, this identifies max{|gamma|+gamma_1 : bar-g^gamma_{alpha,beta}>0} = |alpha|+|beta|+alpha_1+beta_1. (ii) Put N equal to the support maximum established in (i). For n>=N all gamma[n] in the finite positive support are partitions, so the proved all-rank identity is now an ordinary nonnegative Schur expansion; U_{n+k}s_gamma=V^k(U_n s_gamma) there. Thus the whole product is V-stable from N. When N>0, gamma*=alpha+beta is nonempty, its reduced coefficient is 1 by the top-degree lemma and the unique LR tableau, and gamma*[N] has equal positive first two parts. Distinct support tails give distinct Schur labels, so this coefficient does not cancel. Every V(s_mu)=s_{mu+(1)} has first part strictly larger than the second, hence the product at N is not in the image of V. Any putative stabilization index n_0<N would make the product at N equal V^{N-n_0} of its rank-n_0 Jacobi-Trudi-completed product, a contradiction. For both inputs nonempty, N-1 is an ordinary admissible rank; for exactly one empty, N is the minimum ordinary input rank, and no ordinary product below that domain is invoked. If N=0 both inputs are empty: the degreewise internal-product unit h_n=s_(n) gives h_n*h_n=h_n and V^n(1)=h_n, proving threshold zero directly. The two-factor LR first-row inequality used in (i) is explicit: every entry of a nonempty first skew row is 1, since the LR reading word begins at its rightmost (largest) entry and must be lattice; hence the added first-row boxes number at most the 1-content beta_1. Thus lambda_1<=alpha_1+beta_1 for positive c^lambda_{alpha,beta}. Iterating the positive intermediate LR coefficients gives the threefold row inequality. At gamma*=alpha+beta the row-i filling by i is lattice because beta is weakly decreasing; the first row exhausts all beta_1 ones, then the next row exhausts all beta_2 twos, and induction proves uniqueness and coefficient 1.
items.axiom_use: None: the proved finite all-rank expansion, LR row bounds/unique top tableau and the Schur-basis image of V suffice; empty cases are explicit.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 1.2, pp. 4, 8-9
Emmanuel Briand, Amarpreeet Rattan and Mercedes Rosas, On the growth of the Kronecker coefficients, arXiv:1607.02887v1 (2016); Lemma 3.1 and the proof of Proposition 3.2, pp. 9-10

items.title: Murnaghan stability for $\alpha=\beta=(2)$, ranks 4 to 9
items.statement:
For $\alpha=\beta=(2)$ the source's introduction displays the following
internal products $s_{n-2,2}*s_{n-2,2}$ at ranks $n=4,\dots,9$
(notation $s_{a,b,c}$ for Schur functions of the padded partitions, and
$s_\bullet$ on the stable row):

$$s_{2,2}*s_{2,2}=s_4+s_{1,1,1,1}+s_{2,2},$$

$$s_{3,2}*s_{3,2}=s_5+s_{2,1,1,1}+s_{3,2}+s_{4,1}+s_{3,1,1}+s_{2,2,1},$$

$$s_{4,2}*s_{4,2}=s_6+s_{3,1,1,1}+2s_{4,2}+s_{5,1}+s_{4,1,1}+2s_{3,2,1}+s_{2,2,2},$$

$$s_{5,2}*s_{5,2}=s_7+s_{4,1,1,1}+2s_{5,2}+s_{6,1}+s_{5,1,1}+2s_{4,2,1}+s_{3,2,2}+s_{4,3}+s_{3,3,1},$$

$$s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}=s_8+s_{5,1,1,1}+2s_{6,2}+s_{7,1}+s_{6,1,1}+2s_{5,2,1}+s_{4,2,2}+s_{5,3}+s_{4,3,1}+s_{4,4},$$

$$s_{7,2}*s_{7,2}=s_9+s_{6,1,1,1}+2s_{7,2}+s_{8,1}+s_{7,1,1}+2s_{6,2,1}+s_{5,2,2}+s_{6,3}+s_{5,3,1}+s_{5,4},$$

$$s_{\bullet,2}*s_{\bullet,2}=s_\bullet+s_{\bullet,1,1,1}+2s_{\bullet,2}+s_{\bullet,1}+s_{\bullet,1,1}+2s_{\bullet,2,1}+s_{\bullet,2,2}+s_{\bullet,3}+s_{\bullet,3,1}+s_{\bullet,4}.$$

Consequently the reduced coefficients
([[def-reduced-kronecker-coefficient]]) for the pair $((2),(2))$ are
$\bar g^\gamma_{(2),(2)}=1,1,2,1,1,2,1,1,1,1$ for
$\gamma=\varnothing,(1,1,1),(2),(1),(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(3),(3,1),(4)$
respectively, and $\bar g^\gamma_{(2),(2)}=0$ for all other $\gamma$; in
particular $\bar g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2$ and $\bar g^{(4)}_{(2),(2)}=1$. The
displayed data also verify directly, for this pair, that the whole product is
$V$-stable at rank $8$ and not at rank $7$: applying $V$ (adding a box to the
first row of every Schur function) to the rank-$8$ expansion reproduces the
rank-$9$ expansion term by term, whereas applying $V$ to the rank-$7$
expansion misses the single term $s_{4,4}$ of the rank-$8$ expansion, the
other nine terms matching term by term. The proved threshold theorem
([[thm-exact-global-stabilization-threshold-for-a-fixed-kronecker-product]])
establishes $V$-stability for every rank from $8$ onward, with exact least
global index $8=|(2)|+|(2)|+2+2$; the displayed finite data independently
verify the six listed products and the failure of the preceding step.
items.strategy: For every n=4,...,9 compute the actual characters and every Schur coefficient, not merely dimensions. Youngs rule gives M^(n-2,2)=S^(n)+S^(n-1,1)+S^(n-2,2), while the point-permutation module is S^(n)+S^(n-1,1). Hence chi^(n-2,2)=binom(X_1,2)+X_2-X_1, by counting fixed two-element subsets and fixed points. For every partition delta of n, expand s_delta by Jacobi-Trudi and each h_k in power sums; the Frobenius dictionary gives chi^delta(rho)=z_rho[p_rho]s_delta. The tensor multiplicity is sum_{rho partition n}(chi^(n-2,2)(rho))^2 chi^delta(rho)/z_rho, a finite rational sum. Evaluating these finitely many sums gives exactly each displayed product (and zero for unlisted delta). Evaluating these character identities at the identity permutation provides a supplementary dimension check, not the proof of the products. At rank 8 the coefficient of s_(4,4) is 1 and cannot be in the V-image; the other nine shifted rank-7 terms agree with rank 8. General V-stability from 8 and its exact minimality follow from the now-proved threshold theorem, and comparing rank 8 with rank 9 checks the first stable step. The stable reduced list follows from that theorem and the rank-8 decomposition.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Introduction p. 2 (the displayed product table for alpha=beta=(2) at ranks 4 to 9 and the stable row)
I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., Oxford University Press 1995; Chapter I §7 (Frobenius characteristic and character values)

items.title: A global product threshold is not a per-coefficient sharpness claim
items.statement: For alpha=beta=(2) the individual coefficient bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 is already attained at rank 6: the rank-6 product s_{4,2}*s_{4,2} contains 2s_{4,2}, i.e. g^{(4,2)}_{(4,2),(4,2)}=2, which is the stable value bar-g^{(2)}_{(2),(2)}=2 read off from the stable row. Thus this single coefficient stops growing strictly before the whole product stabilizes: the rank-7 and rank-8 products still contain 2s_{5,2} and 2s_{6,2} respectively, matching the stable value, while the whole product is not even V-stable at rank 7 (applying V to s_{5,2}*s_{5,2} misses the term s_{4,4} occurring in s_{6,2}*s_{6,2}) and only becomes V-stable at rank 8. Therefore the exact global product threshold (the least rank from which the whole product is V-stable) is not a per-coefficient sharpness statement: single coefficients may stabilize earlier, and no claim that a coefficient first becomes stable at the global threshold is valid.
items.strategy: Verification from the source's displayed products: read the coefficient of s_{4,2} in s_{4,2}*s_{4,2} (equal to 2), the coefficients of s_{5,2} and s_{6,2} in the ranks 7 and 8 products (2 in both cases), and the stable coefficient 2s_{bullet,2} in the stable row; compare the ranks 6,7,8 products under the operator V (V of the rank-7 product equals the rank-8 product minus the single term s_{4,4}). This shows the stabilization rank of the single coefficient (2) is at most 6, strictly below the global V-stability rank 8. The counterexample does not use the general threshold theorem; it is a finite boundary witness warning against quantifying the global threshold as a sharp per-coefficient bound. To justify constancy for every later rank, use the proved threshold through the example: all ranks n>=8 have the stable coefficient 2, and the explicit ranks 6 and7 already have that value. The rank 5 value is1 by the verified product table. Thus this coefficient has stabilization rank 6, strictly below the whole-product threshold 8; it is not inferred solely from matching adjacent products.

references.title: Emmanuel Briand, Rosa Orellana and Mercedes Rosas, The stability of the Kronecker product of Schur functions, arXiv:0907.4652v2 (2009); Introduction p. 2 (displayed products for alpha=beta=(2)) and section 3 pp. 8-9 (the sharp product threshold)
